question.leadin: Answer the following about the Gaza Strip.
question.text: In 1993, Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization signed a series of accords named for this city, the capital of Norway. The accords gave Palestinians the right to self-government in Gaza.
question.clue: Works such as Monolith, which is a tower of human bodies, and Wheel of Life are contained in this city's Frogner Park, which features other stone and bronze statuary by Gustav Vigeland .

swap.leadin: Answer the following about German invasions during World War II.
swap.text: Germany invaded this country and Denmark as part of Operation Weserubung. This country was home to German heavy water production and was led by Vidkun Quisling after its surrender.
swap.clue: A parliamentary debate nicknamed for this country involved Leo Amery quoting Cromwell's command "In the name of God, go!", leading to the resignation of Neville Chamberlain.

question.leadin: The Treaty of Nystad ended this war in 1721, 12 years after a decisive victory over Charles XII at Poltava ended Sweden's time as a European power.
question.text: Name this war motivated by one European power's desire for a port city on the Baltic Sea.
question.clue: During this war, one side relieved a siege during a snowstorm at the Battle of Narva.

swap.leadin: This member of the House of Vasa defeated Count Tilly in his most famous victory, Breitenfeld.
swap.text: Name this man who died at the Battle of Lutzen and was known as the "Lion of the North."
swap.answerHtml: Gustavus Adolphus [or Gustav Adolf; Gustav II; Gustavus the Great; prompt on “Gustav” or “Gustavus”]
swap.clue: In addition to ending the Kalmar War, one military rival to this person employed an elector named Maximilian I that died with him at Ingolstadt after losing to the numerically superior force of this ruler at the Battle of the Rain.

question.text: During the 1600s, Sweden was led by this philosophically-minded queen, the daughter of Gustavus Adolphus. Peter Minuit established a fort named for her in the New World.
question.clue: Although historians are not sure whether the abdication was influenced by a clandestine love for Cardinal Decio Azzolino, we do know that this ruler received educateion from Jorge Stiernhelm.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about people whose names have become synonymous with the word traitor.
swap.text: This man collaborated with the Germans after the invasion of his country, and requested to be made the 'Fuhrer of Norway'. He was found guilty of high treason by the allies and sentenced to death after the war.
swap.clue: This politician launched their political career in a series of articles explaining their 'political thoughts' on the death of mentor Fritjohf Nansen.
swap.set: 2023 Politics & History with a side of Memes

question.leadin: This institution was formed when Margaret I of Denmark's great-nephew, Erik of Pomerania, was crowned on Trinity Sunday.
question.text: Name this Nordic union established to counter the influence of the Hanseatic League. Internal conflict in this polity occurred primarily between Danish and Swedish "protectors of the realm" such as Sten Sture the Elder.
question.clue: Members of the Sture family served as regents to this state, which was targeted by the Engelbrekt rising.

swap.leadin: This king and his father Gormr set up the Jelling ("yelling") Stones in honor of Gormr and his wife Thyrve.
swap.text: Name this King of Denmark with a colorful nickname, whose Jelling Stone suggests was the first king of a unified Denmark.
swap.clue: This ruler was captured by the possibly fictional Styrbjorn the Strong.

question.leadin: It arose over the control of the Hanko naval base and was prosecuted by the coalition government of Risto Ryti.
question.text: Name this war which saw the use of the Mannerheim line in an attempt to repel a Soviet invasion.
question.clue: One sniper in this war had 505 confirmed kills, earning him the nickname "White Death".

swap.text: Before losing at Hastings, Harold had defeated and killed this king of Norway at the Battle of Stamford Bridge.
swap.clue: This man married the daughter of Yaroslav the Wise, Elisiv of Kiev, on his return from Constantinople.

question.leadin: Name these men who have held the position of UN Secretary-General.
question.text: This Norwegian was the first man to serve as UN Secretary-General. He ran afoul of the Soviets for supporting UN involvement in the Korean War and of Joseph McCarthy, who accused him of supporting anti-US subversion.
question.clue: Hammarskjold's predecessor as secretary general was this Norwegian, who ceased to be recognized as secretary general by the Soviet Union due to the UN's involvement in the Korean War.

swap.leadin: Many of this body's members were chieftains called godar who served in a law council called the Logretta.
swap.text: Name this body established in 930. This body assembled at a rocky outcrop called the Logberg, and was presided over by an official called the Lawspeaker who served a three-year term.
swap.clue: It was disbanded in favor of the High Court from 1800 to 1845, when Christian VIII allowed it to reconvene.

question.leadin: Cardinal Mazarin remarked that if all the ministers of Europe were on the same boat, this person would be at the helm.
question.text: Name this Swedish politician. He served as regent for Gustavus Adolphus in his absence and, after his death in battle, regent for his young daughter Christina.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of the good old-fashioned fun of throwing sticks.
swap.text: The stick throwing game of skittles originated in a region this country shares with its eastern neighbour. A bat sport invented by a veteran of this country's Civil War was demonstrated when it hosted the 1952 Summer Olympics.
swap.clue: This country was forced to expel German soldiers by the Moscow Armistice, in which it also ceded Karelia to its eastern neighbour.

question.text: The second False Dmitriy lost many of his supporters after the intervention of Sigismund III of the Poland-Lithuania Commonwealth, who used the confusion of the Time of Troubles as an attempt to conquer parts of Russia. Sigismund belonged to this royal house, founded after Gustav I revolted against Christian II and the Kalmar Union.
question.clue: A queen from this royal house abdicated after converting to Catholicism and housed Descartes in his final years.

swap.leadin: The Academy Award for the Best Film in a Foreign Language is the only Oscar awarded to an entire country.
swap.text: Which country was awarded the Foreign Language Oscar in two successive years, first for Babette's Feast in 1987 and then for Pelle the Conqueror in 1988?
swap.clue: This country that still controls the territories of the Faroe Islands and Greenland.

question.leadin: This erector of the Jelling Stones was the first Danish king to be baptized.
question.text: Name this unifier of Denmark, the son of Gorm the Old.

swap.leadin: This older brother of Haakon VII of Norway is the only man to ever be king of Iceland.
swap.text: Name this Danish king who resisted German occupation during World War II and reportedly wore a yellow star to sup-port Jews.
swap.answerHtml: <u>Christian X</u> [or <u>Christian Carl Frederik Albert Alexander Vilhelm</u>; prompt on “Christian”]
swap.clue: In addition to Vilhelm Buhl, another prime minister who served under this king was deposed after failing to call a referendum regarding the return of Flensburg to his country, and that prime minister was named Carl Theodor Zahle.

question.text: In August of 1944 Mannerheim succeeded this man as president of Finland when the parliament deposed this man and appointed Mannerheim in his place.
question.clue: This prime minister of Finland who resigned and was replaced by Carl Mannerheim in 1944.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Finland during World War II.
swap.text: Paavo Tavela is one of only a handful of recipients of the highest Finnish military honor named after this man, a former president of Finland whose name is given to the line that delineates the Karelian isthmus from Russia.
swap.clue: During World War I, Finnish independence advocates often joined the German army as Jagers, a movement that this Finnish Baron opposed. This man names a fortification line built by the Finns during the Winter War.
